main_text.p: I. Genera quoque in hac declinatione se habent, ut in praecedente, ut: ὁ λεὼς, ἡ ἄλως, ὁ ἡ ἡ ἀγεως, τὸ ἀγεων.
[Unicum in ως neutrum est: τὸ ἄζεως.]
II. Genitivus, definit in ω. ut: ἡ νεω, ἀνώγεω. [Poëtæ adjiciunt o: ut, τᾶ πεπω, πεπωο.]
Dativus. in ω. ut: τῷ νεω, ἀνώγεω.
Accusativus, in ων. ut: τὴν νεων, τὸ ἀνώγεων.
III. [Quinque sunt, quæ Accusativum sine v finiunt: ἄθως, ἄϑω: ἔως, ἔω: κέως, κέω, & contracte κῶς, κῶ: τέως, τέω: λαγῶς, λαγῶ.]
II. Vocativus est similis Nominativo: prout omnis atticus in quacunque declinatione. ut: ὦ νεως, ἀνώγεων.
In duali Numero: Nominativus, Accusativus, & Vocativus, definunt in ω. ut: τὼ νεω, ἀνώγεω.
Genitivus & Dativus, in ων. ut: τὴν νεων, ἀνώγεων.
In plurali: Nominativus & Vocativus reliqui, in ω: neuter, in ω. ut: οἱ νεω, τὰ ἀνώγεω.
Genitivus, in ων. ut: τῶν νεῶν, ἀνώγεων.
Dativus, in ως. ut: τοῖς νεως, ἀνώγεως.
Accusativi reliqui, in ως: neuter, in ω. ut: τὰς νεως, τὰ ἀνώγεω.

page.notes: Greek accents and some breathings are rendered approximately; several Greek words in the margin-free lines are uncertain. The printed catchword "Quæ-" at the foot is treated as a catchword-like fragment in the text.
